institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The surrounding nature and travels destinations

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nice student environment and the intro week, made it possible to meet all the new exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the info was okay, but a little bit confusing with which documents you should upload to student web.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The only assistance I got was help with which courses I could select.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got my housing really late, due to there not being enough student housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The transport around Tromsø is really easy and bus is cheap, so I think the student housing seems quite nice no matter where on Tromsø you live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was happy with my student housing, no deposit, it was cheap and had some nice roomies.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was submitting some documents to student web, which could be a little bit confusing. But overall it went nicely.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Questions regarding whatever you did not understand.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull, I got just the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe to ask if they are confused about anything, but also the webside has some nice pages for the exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 2 bachelor courses and 1 master course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was very similar. We had lectures and seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MBI-2004 Immunology, PSY-1004 Biological Psychology and BIO-3015 Arctic marine system ecology and climate change.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Arctic course was really nice, very interesting and cool to learn about the arctic biology while being here.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Had to buy all the kitchen stuff for my housing, such as pots and pans, plates, knife, forks, glass. There was basically nothing when I arrived, so it was a little bit expensive to buy everything you need to cook. Beside buying kitchen stuff I had to buy curtains, a duvet and pillow.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Less expensive is transport on Tromsø, that's quite cheap to go around by bus. More expensive is the food like fresh greens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice with the weekly email to let us know what is planned the following week.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a fitness at uni, which has free yoga once a week. There is many different social stuff, like vintage market and many other stuff.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend to just enjoy the nature. Go hiking in the weekend, go skiing on Tromsø and just enjoy. Tromsø and its surroundings has so much to offer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking on Kvaløya, Senja and in Tromsdalen. Take some nice trips to go around the area, its absolutely amazing nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, many things in Norway is like in Denmark, which I thought was really nice and home like.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out in the weekends and attend class, then I think its quite natural to meet the local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate that the norwegian is quite similar to danish. Its easy to understand and to meet and socialize with the locals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The nature (absolutely amazing), The student environment, The school.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Useful is to apply for housing quite quickly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The traveling around and living in such beautiful nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The housing was a little bit difficult in the beginning, due to the samskipnaden making a few mistakes with the key and the cleaning of my room. But everything worked out it was really nice.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
